source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "ដំណាំសណ្តែកដី" (Peanut / Groundnut Cultivation handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, 2008, produced under Loan 2022-CAM(SF) (an ADB-financed project; the cover names a livelihood/agriculture-improvement program under this loan). Uploaded as a 14-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source B for crop/peanut in this knowledge base (Source A was a shorter ECOSORN leaflet processed in Batch 42).
text: The source states peanut is affected by disease and insect pressures broadly similar to soybean and mung bean. Leaf-spot disease (Cercospora) is named as a common disease, producing leaf lesions that can cause leaf drop; the source estimates yield loss from this disease at roughly 20% in affected fields, and describes control via spraying a product named "Minagro," applied (per the source) at roughly 2 sachets mixed into 18 liters of water, on an interval described as roughly weekly (7 days). A virus disease referred to as "Rosette" is also described, causing stunted growth and poor or absent pod set when infection occurs early; it is spread by an insect vector (aphid), and the source recommends controlling the vector with a product named "Diazinon," applied at roughly 2 sachets mixed into 18 liters of water. A leaf-feeding caterpillar pest is also pictured and described in general terms as feeding on foliage; as with other pests, the source recommends removing and destroying visibly infested plants to slow spread.
caveat: "Minagro" and "Diazinon" are printed in the source as product/brand-style names rather than as standard chemical active-ingredient names (Diazinon is itself an organophosphate active ingredient, but 'Minagro' is a commercial product name whose active ingredient is not stated in the source); both are reported here as printed rather than mapped to a specific active ingredient that was not confirmed in the text. Dosage and interval figures are also reported as printed.
